history.commentary: Heather Siegers to Nahida Akter - OUT! CAUGHT! Nahida swings for the hills but finds Kalis at deep midwicket. Heather Siegers takes another wicket in the decisive last over and with that, Netherlands Women have beaten Bangladesh Women for the first time ever. The fact that these two teams are placed in the same group in the upcoming ICC Women's T20 World Cup increases the significance of this result. On a length, outside off. The batter stepped out and tried to wallop this one away — she had no other option. But she could not clear the tall lady at the brink of the boundary. Joyous scenes unfold as the Dutch get together to exchange high-fives, hugs and smiles. A great result for them.

history.commentary: 8:38 PM IST and 4:08 PM Local Time: Netherlands win by 8 runs! It has been a fine performance from the Dutch! Bangladesh fought valiantly in the form of their Captain but that is all. No other batter could contribute and they fell agonizingly close in this chase! Bangladesh won the toss and elected to field first. The Dutch openers were up to the challenge and they started off in fine fashion. Heather Siegers (52 off 43) in particular played a fine knock. She stitched two really valuable partnerships with Phebe Molkenboer (29 off 24) and then with Sterre Kalis (28 off 27). The Netherlands were bossing the contest with 115 on the board. Bangladesh did strike back to back and brought the score to 116/3. However, a powerful finish from the likes of Babette de Leede (16 off 7) and Robine Rijke (18 off 10) powered the Dutch to a formidable total of 162/5! The pick of the bowlers was Fariha Trisna with 2-26 in her spell. The chase was always going to be a stiff one as Bangladesh had never chased anything above 150 in the past. It did not start in the best fashion. The Dutch new ball bowlers were effective and reduced Bangladesh to 13/2. Nigar Sultana and Juairiya Ferdous added 37 for the third wicket. However, that is when Ferdous fell. The Dutch once again regained control and continued to strike. Nigar Sultana was scoring decently from one end. However she found no support from the other end. Further wickets tumbled regularly and Bangladesh were down to 117/5 . Nigar got to her 50 but as I mentioned without great support from the other end. The equation came down to 30 off 2 overs and further to 18 off 6 balls. The task was so stiff that eventually Bangladesh lost 3 wickets in the final over including the one of Nigar for 77. They fell 8 runs short. The pick of the bowlers was Heather Siegers for her 3-39 in 4 overs.

history.commentary: 9:46 PM IST & 5:16 PM Local Time: A superb all-round performance from Gloucestershire as they bring an end to Yorkshire's three-match winning streak. Gloucestershire seal a convincing 56-run victory here at Headingley. Earlier in the evening, Gloucestershire won the toss and chose to bat first, making a strong start despite losing Miles Hammond for 13 in the fourth over to Moeen Ali. They reached 43/1 at the end of the Powerplay before D'Arcy Short and Joseph Phillips took charge with a superb 95-run partnership that put the visitors firmly on top. Phillips played an important hand of 42 off 25 balls before falling in the 13th over, while D'Arcy Short continued to dominate the bowling attack, accelerating brilliantly after his fifty and eventually departing for a magnificent 82 off 50 balls. Although Gloucestershire lost wickets at regular intervals in the closing overs and surrendered some momentum, a late cameo from Duan Jansen, who remained unbeaten on 12 off 9 balls and struck three successive boundaries in the final over, helped propel them to an imposing 217/6 from their 20 overs. In reply, Yorkshire needed an explosive start in pursuit of the daunting target and Adam Lyth did his best to provide exactly that. The left-hander came out with positive intent and kept the scoreboard moving, but wickets kept tumbling at the other end. Jonny Bairstow, William Luxton and James Wharton all fell cheaply inside the Powerplay as Yorkshire adopted an all-out attacking approach. Despite the setbacks, they raced to 65/3 at the end of 6 overs , keeping themselves in the hunt. From there, it was almost a one-man show from Adam Lyth. The opener fought a lone battle and carried Yorkshire's hopes throughout the chase while wickets continued to fall around him. Apart from Lyth, only two other batters managed to reach double figures as the required rate kept climbing steadily. Lyth tried his best to take the game deep and remained aggressive even as the pressure mounted. He looked set for a well-deserved century but eventually fell for a magnificent 97 off 56 balls after batting deep into the innings. Yorkshire were eventually bowled out for 161 in 17.4 overs, handing Gloucestershire a convincing 56-run victory. D'Arcy Short capped off a brilliant all-round performance with the ball, finishing with outstanding figures of 4/31 .

history.commentary: Preview by AkshayaKrishna Polya After a comprehensive seven-wicket win in the rain-curtailed series opener in Dharamsala on Saturday, India will now aim to take an unassailable lead in this three-match ODI series when they take the field against Afghanistan in the second game at Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium , Lucknow, on Wednesday (June 17). It took more than four hours for the officials, players and the fans to witness some action after relentless rain at the picturesque venue in the foothills of the Himalayas. The contest was reduced to a 25-over-per-side game. India won the toss and decided to bowl first, which was a no-brainer in a shortened match. India's new-ball bowlers Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh reduced Afghanistan to 26/3 inside the five-over powerplay, but Rahmanullah Gurbaz had other ideas. The wicketkeeper batter teed off from the get-go and scored a 48-ball century, the fastest for Afghanistan in the ODIs. However, he was cleaned up soon by Nitish Kumar Reddy, who broke the 116-run partnership that Gurbaz stitched with his skipper Hashmatullah Shahidi. Reddy and debutants Harsh Dubey & Brar then bowled brilliantly in the slog overs to pull things back and bundle out Afghanistan for 194 inside the allotted 25 overs. The Men in Blue were off to a flying start, with Azmatullah Omarzai failing to control the swing up front. He also hit Rohit Sharma on his right wrist in the first over, but the former Indian skipper battled with the injury to hit run-a-ball 16 before getting run out, courtesy of a mix-up with Shubman Gill just after the powerplay. Gill and Ishan Kishan went hammer and tongs to bring the required run rate under control with a 70-run stand. Rashid Khan outfoxed Kishan with a wrong 'un and knocked him over for a 22-ball 34. Shreyas Iyer couldn't get going. The Indian captain had very little pressure on him as he hit some stylish strokes during his glorious 84 off just 66 balls, but KL Rahul later took the limelight and also hit the finishing runs with an unbeaten 39 off just 19 balls. There is no rain on the radar for the matchday. Traditionally, Ekana aids spin bowling, and India might bring in Kuldeep Yadav in place of Prasidh Krishna , who wasn't at his best in the first ODI. On the other hand, Darwish Rasooli, who missed the previous ODI due to a family bereavement, has rejoined the team in Lucknow. Can Afghanistan win their maiden ODI against India and force a decider, or will the hosts prove to be too good for the tourists once again? To know, join us at 12:30 PM IST, Local Time, on Wednesday for its live coverage!

history.commentary: Preview by AkshayaKrishna Polya Bangladesh 's capital went bonkers when they thumped Australia in the ODI series earlier this month. It was the first time that the Tigers managed to hunt down the Kangaroos in an ODI series. However, a Cooper Connolly special in the third ODI upstaged Shoriful Islam's six-fer before Adam Zampa hit the winning runs to deny the hosts a rare chance of a whitewash. The focus now shifts to the shortest format, with Bir Sreshtho Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman Stadium in Chattogram hosting the T20Is. The series opener will take place on Wednesday (June 17). The Aussies have now lost back-to-back ODI series in the subcontinent in the absence of several key players. However, the tourists are bolstered by the arrival of the skipper Mitchell Marsh. He missed the last two ODI series due to an ankle injury he sustained while playing for Lucknow Super Giants in the Indian Premier League. However, the 2021 T20 World Champions will be without some of their senior players. Speedsters Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins remain rested, while Travis Head was a late pull-out from the tour and has also been rested. Tanveer Sangha has been ruled out due to a hamstring injury he picked up in the ODIs against Pakistan. The all-rounders Marcus Stoinis and Glenn Maxwell have been left out because the visitors are looking to give young players a chance to build a team for the future. Cameron Green, who was previously selected for the entire tour, has now been rested, given a long home summer coming up. It gives the youngster, Joel Davies , who was sensational with his all-round prowess for Sydney Sixers, a chance to showcase his talent at the highest level, as he received a maiden call-up. The firepower of Tim David and wicketkeeper batter Josh Inglis , who led in the ODIs, are the experienced batters in the lineup, while Adam Zampa will lead the spin attack alongside the seamers Nathan Ellis and Xavier Bartlett . Spencer Johnson returns after a long injury lay-off and is fresh off some IPL experience with Chennai Super Kings. Riley Meredith, who recently made his international comeback after a stellar Big Bash season with Hobart Hurricanes, is also in the squad. All-rounder Aaron Hardie , left-arm spinner Matthew Kuhnemann , middle-order batter Matt Renshaw , wicketkeeper batter Josh Philippe and Cooper Connolly , fresh off a match-winning 149, make it a good bunch of talented players. India-born all-rounder Nikhil Chaudhary , who has been brilliant for the Hurricanes in the BBL, has received a maiden call-up, following Head's withdrawal. On the flip side, Bangladesh, despite being a strong suit at home and coming off a famous 2-1 ODI series win over their counterparts, have some injuries to deal with in the camp. Skipper Litton Das , who suffered a leg injury in the third ODI and was also retired hurt at one stage, remains in doubt for the series opener. A call on his participation will be taken very close to the toss. As a result, Soumya Sarkar has been added to the squad as a cover. Promising middle-order batter Towhid Hridoy is the vice-captain and most probably will come out to lead the side if Das is unavailable. In addition, Parvez Hossain Emon is ill and could miss the first T20I. The pace trio - Taskin Ahmed , Mustafizur Rahman and Nahid Rana - have all made a comeback into the T20I side after missing the previous series against New Zealand. That meant the likes of Tanzim Hasan Sakib , Ripon Mondal and Mohammad Saifuddin were dropped. However, whether Bangla Tigers field all three seamers is a question they will answer at the toss, as Shoriful Islam, who has been doing a fine job in the shortest format and is fresh off a brilliant six-wicket haul in the last ODI, is expected to retain his place. Bangladesh will heavily rely on the likes of Tanzid Hasan Tamim , Saif Hassan , Hridoy and Shamim Hossain with the bat, while b will be the backup gloveman in the side.
